svg.aria-label: The bear toe line test on a front track. Step 1: lay a straight edge across the top of the front palm pad. Step 2: look at the small outer toe. Black bear: toes in a curved row, the small outer toe falls below the line, short claws close to the toes, 2.5 to 6.4 cm ahead. Grizzly: toes in a straighter row, all 5 sit above the line, long claw marks far ahead of the toes, 5 to 11.4 cm. Grizzly until proven otherwise.

g.data-tip: 1. The straight edge|Lay a straight edge across the top of the palm pad, under the toes (70%). Idaho Fish and Game: on a grizzly it will not cross the toes; on a black bear it crosses them (80%).
g.text: Line across top of the palm pad

g.data-tip: 2. Clean prints only|Snow melt can change a track's shape; look for clean prints (85%).
Black bear track|5 toes in a curved row; the outer, smallest toe falls below the line (70%). Front track about 10 to 16 cm long and 10 to 14 cm wide (70%).
Black bear claws|Short claws, about 3 to 5 cm, print as dots close to the toes (70%). Middle claw marks sit 2.5 to 6.4 cm (1 to 2.5 in) ahead of the toe pads (80%).
Grizzly track|Toes in a straighter row; all 5 sit above the line (70%). Front track about 18 cm long and 13 cm wide (65%).
Grizzly claws|Claw marks sit well ahead of the toes (65%). Middle claw marks are 5 to 11.4 cm (2 to 4.5 in) ahead of the toe pads (80%).

Grizzly until proven otherwise|A bear track with long claw marks and toes in a straight row: make noise, keep bear spray on your belt, and do not follow it. A fresh grizzly track on your trail means change your plan (Tip).
